subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public phase, stagger, or prime-cadence controls for cron `every` schedules, or keep `every` as a fixed anchored interval and limit anti-herd behavior to heartbeat plus cron expressions?
rationale: The remaining work changes public scheduling semantics and persisted config/API shape, and repository policy treats config/default and setup surfaces as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
options.body: Add one explicit interval scheduling contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep every fixed
options.body: Preserve current fixed anchored `every` semantics and rely on heartbeat phase plus cron-expression stagger for anti-herd behavior.

options.title: Adopt broader prime mode
options.body: Accept a larger product surface covering prime cadence transforms and deterministic phase controls for both heartbeat and cron, with migration and observability requirements.

recommendation.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
recommendation.body: Add one explicit interval scheduling contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current cron stagger surface and are the strongest routing candidate for the remaining cron scheduling API boundary.
